newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Bradesco Seguros 1996 net profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Bradesco Seguros 1996 net profit rises.

text.p: Profits at Brazil's Bradesco Seguros jumped 43.54 percent in 1996 to 353.3 million reais ($337.3 million) from 246.1 million reais the previous year, a company official said.

Bradesco Seguros, which is controlled by Brazil's largest private bank Bradesco, posted premiums of 2.8 billion reais, an increase of 19 percent over 1995, said Bradesco Seguros president Ararino de Oliveira.
Bradesco Seguros is the largest insurance firm in Brazil, but it posted in 1996 one of the highest earnings in the country's insurance sector, according to Oliveira.
He said 1996 results were boosted by profitable operations in pension and capitalization plans, a growing market in Brazil.
For this year, the company expects to continue expanding services and it plans to launch life insurance products in the second half of 1997.
